name: Micron Technology
day_summary: SATURDAY WEEKEND REVIEW — US MARKETS CLOSED; $1,132.33 LAST CLOSE (JUNE 26, −6.69%); BLOWOUT-EARNINGS GIVE-BACK CONTINUES IN A RISK-OFF TAPE. No US equity trading June 27 (Saturday). MU last traded at $1,132.33 (June 26, −$81.23, −6.69% from the $1,213.56 June 25 close). The two-day arc tells the story: a record fiscal-Q3 print (EPS $25.11, revenue $41.46B, Q4 guide ~$50B at ~86% gross margin) ran the stock up into the June 25 close near its highs, and June 26 gave a big chunk of it back as the entire AI-memory complex sold off — SK Hynix fell −8.36% on a KOSPI dual-circuit-breaker session and the broad regime turned risk-off (SPX 7,354, below the 7,460 floor; VIX ~18.41, above the 17 gate). This is 'sell the news on a sold-out story' meeting a macro air-pocket, not a thesis break. The fundamentals are firing on every cylinder; the tape is simply digesting a near-10x run into a hostile week (NFP July 2, markets closed July 3). Day winner: BEARS — the fade-the-blowout trade and the macro risk-off both paid.
long_pnl: longs are still sitting on enormous gains — MU is up ~11x off its 52-week low ($103.38) — but gave back $81/share on June 26 as the post-earnings high was sold into; the position is a hold-the-cycle trade now, not an add here; the SK Hynix ADR confirmation (Nasdaq July 10) validates the HBM complex MU sells into, but provides no near-term price support before the macro week clears
short_pnl: shorts pressing the 'priced for perfection after a 10x run' thesis had their best session yet: −6.69% on June 26 rewarded fading the blowout into the risk-off tape; the structural short remains painful against an 86% gross-margin guide and a sold-out HBM order book, so this is a tactical win inside a strong fundamental uptrend, not a thesis confirmation

decision.horizon: 1–2 quarters · into the fiscal-Q4 print (~late Sept 2026) and the HBM4 ramp
decision.rationale: HOLD at MEDIUM conviction — UNCHANGED. The business could hardly be better: the Q4 guide implies ~$50B revenue at ~86% gross margin, HBM is effectively sold out into 2027, and CEO Sanjay Mehrotra says memory tightness is 'locked in to persist beyond calendar 2027.' On forward earnings the stock is not expensive (a ~$31 quarterly EPS run-rate keeps the P/E in the low double digits even here). But two things argue against adding into this week: (1) the tape already discounted the blowout — a record print produced a high that was promptly sold, and June 26 erased −6.69%; (2) the macro is hostile — regime gates breached, SK Hynix in circuit-breaker territory, and an NFP binary July 2 into a 3-day holiday gap. New money waits for the $1,030–$1,080 shelf to prove itself or a confirmed close back above the June 25 high; existing holders ride the cycle with a trailing stop, because memory is cyclical and this is the part of the cycle where the prints are best. The read-through to our SK Hynix desk remains strongly positive — and the SK Hynix $29.4B ADR is third-party validation of exactly the HBM demand Micron is printing.

outlook.short_term: Choppy-to-lower near term. The blowout was discounted, IV is collapsing, the stock just gave back −6.69%, and the macro week is hostile (NFP July 2 into the July 3 close). Expect a range between the $1,030–$1,080 shelf and the June 25 high (~$1,213) until the macro clears; a decisive break of either end sets the next leg. Monday June 29 will trade off the SK Hynix/KOSPI reaction to the ADR and the broad risk-on/off tape as much as anything Micron-specific.
outlook.long_term: Structurally constructive. If memory tightness persists beyond 2027 and HBM4 ramps into Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, Micron is printing peak-cycle cash at high margins and the forward multiple is undemanding. The risk is not the next two quarters but the eventual cycle turn — memory always mean-reverts. Own it as a cyclical with a plan to trim into euphoria, not a buy-and-forget compounder; the SK Hynix ADR and Micron's own $50B guide are the cleanest evidence the AI-memory super-cycle is real and broadening.

analysis: Micron's fiscal Q3 was about as good as a memory print gets — a 24% EPS beat, record revenue, and a sequential guide to $50B at 86% gross margin — and within two sessions the stock gave back −6.69%. That divergence is the actionable signal. When a clean blowout off a sold-out order book is sold into and then hit by a macro air-pocket (SK Hynix circuit breakers, regime gates breached), the market is telling you the cycle's good news is largely discounted and that future returns come from the *duration* of the up-cycle, not its existence. The bull case is genuinely strong and, importantly, cheap on forward numbers; the bear case is simply that you are buying peak earnings in a cyclical into a hostile week. The right posture for most investors is to hold, let the $1,030–$1,080 shelf prove itself, and use Micron — alongside the SK Hynix $29.4B ADR — as the cleanest confirmation that the AI-memory super-cycle our SK Hynix desk tracks is real and broadening. Do not chase; let it come to you.

so_what.line: If you hold Micron, hold and don't chase — the business just printed a record quarter and guided to ~$50B, but the stock already ran on it and gave −6.7% back Friday in a risk-off tape; ride the cycle with a trailing stop and let new money wait for the $1,030–$1,080 shelf.
so_what.bull: A $50B guide at 86% margins with HBM sold out past 2027 is peak-cycle cash, and it's still cheap on forward earnings.
so_what.bear: It's a cyclical at peak margins after a near-10x run — it will de-rate fast the day guidance softens, and the macro week is hostile.
